issues.issue: This recital says Certificates are transferred as 'partial consideration', but the operative Acquisition Price definition in Section 1 fixes consideration as cash only and Section 2(c) speaks of delivering 'the Securities'. What the total consideration consists of is left to be reconciled across recital and operative text.

The recital assigns servicing to GreenPoint, while the operative Purchase Price definition contemplates 'if the HELOC Seller is also the servicer' and Sections 7(ii) and 7(sss) warrant about an undefined 'Servicer'. Who the Servicer is for purposes of those provisions has to be reconciled with this recital.

This recital says the representations and the remedies for their breach pass to the Issuer only 'to the extent provided in the related Assignment Agreement', whereas the closing paragraphs of Section 7 state the representations inure to the Purchaser 'its successors and assigns' without qualification. Who may enforce the repurchase remedy turns on reconciling the two.

This clause imports undefined capitalized terms from the Sale and Servicing Agreement, yet Section 7 uses terms ('Revolving Credit Loan', 'Revolving Credit Loan Schedule', 'Mortgage Interest Rate', 'Securities') that sit alongside this Agreement's own definitions of 'HELOCs', 'Mortgage Loan Schedule' and 'Mortgage Rate'. Whether the imported and locally defined terms are the same thing is a live construction question.
The price is left as '$ * __ (plus $ * in accrued interest)', so the amount of the Acquisition Price cannot be determined from the face of the definition. The essential consideration term is blank.

'Scheduled Payment' is not defined in this Agreement, so the Due Date is fixed by reference to a term that must be found elsewhere. Section 7(hh) separately says Minimum Monthly Payments are due on the first day of each month.

'a flow loan purchase agreement' is unidentified and undated, so which HELOCs are EMC Flow Loans cannot be determined from the definition. The category matters because Section 4(b) carves EMC Flow Loans out of the document-delivery substitutions.

The definition is circular: HELOCs are 'any of the HELOCs that are identified as such on the Mortgage Loan Schedule', so the pool is defined only by the schedule the HELOC Seller prepares. Its content is fixed outside the four corners of the Agreement.

'Mortgage' is limited to an instrument creating a lien on 'an interest in an estate in fee simple', but Sections 7(k), 7(mm) and 7(zz) expressly contemplate HELOCs secured by leasehold estates and ground leases. Whether leasehold-secured loans are within the defined collateral cannot be resolved from the definition alone.
'as stated herein' is a mechanical error: no interest rate is stated in this Agreement, and the rate is necessarily stated in the Mortgage Note ('therein'). The definition therefore points nowhere.

Clause (iii) reads 'any costs and damages (if any) incurred by the Trust in connection with any violation of the terms of such HELOC of any anti-predatory lending laws', which is ungrammatical and leaves unclear whose violation of what is compensated. The netting provisions in (i) and (ii) also apply only 'if the HELOC Seller is also the servicer', a contingency the recitals say does not obtain.

'the same or higher credit quality characteristics' and 'a maximum Mortgage Rate determined in accordance with then current underwriting standards' set no measurable benchmark for eligibility of a substitute loan. Whether a proffered loan qualifies is left to argument.

Value is the lesser of the appraised value and 'the sales price of such property at the time of origination', but a HELOC secured by a property the borrower already owns has no sales price at origination. For refinance loans the formula has no second input.

This subsection conditions the sale on 'the conditions set forth in Section 11 hereof', but the conditions to closing are in Section 10 (Section 11 is Fees and Expenses) and Section 2(c) correctly cites Section 10. The two subsections of the same section point at different conditions provisions.

'the Securities' is never defined in this Agreement, which separately defines the Notes and the Certificates, so what the Purchaser must deliver alongside the Acquisition Price is uncertain. The recital speaks only of 'Certain Certificates'.

The phrase 'and all payments thereof' is attached to both sentences, so on its face the Purchaser is entitled to all payments and the HELOC Seller is also entitled to all payments. The allocation of collections around the Cut-off Date is left self-contradictory.

The 'in lieu of' clauses are ungrammatical (clause (i) never completes its subject), so which documents may be substituted for which, and the reach of the 'other than the Mortgages related to the EMC Flow Loans' carve-out, is not determinable from the text. The substitution regime for delivery is the operative obligation.

This subsection recites that 'the Master Servicer agrees that it will not' alter the MERS codes, but the Preamble makes only EMC and the Purchaser parties to this Agreement. Whether a non-party can be bound by this covenant is a question the instrument as a whole raises.

The acknowledgment that the HELOCs 'will ultimately be assigned' to the Indenture Trustee 'on the date hereof' is internally inconsistent as to timing, mixing a future assignment with a same-day one. It is unclear whether it states a present transfer or an expectation.

'from time to time', 'upon reasonable request' and 'such due diligence as any such party reasonably believes is appropriate' set no boundary on the HELOC Seller's file-access and personnel obligations. The extent of the access duty is left to be argued.

The first sentence requires the Custodian to review the Mortgage Files and certify that documents have been executed, received and relate to the scheduled HELOCs, while the last sentence says the Custodian has 'no duty or obligation to inspect, review or examine said documents'. The two sentences of the same subsection cannot both be given full effect.

The HELOC Seller must cure a Material Defect 'within 90 days from the date of notice' and, if it does not, must substitute or repurchase 'within 90 days of the date of notice' — the same period, so the cure period and the repurchase period run out together. The sequencing of the remedy is self-contradictory.

'MOM Loan' is used as the trigger for excusing recording evidence but is nowhere defined in this Agreement, and the same subsection labels its exceptions '(a)' and '(b)' inside a subsection already lettered '(a)'. The scope of the recording exception is left uncertain.

The failure to record is deemed a Material Defect to which 'the provisions of Section 5(c) and (d) shall apply', but Section 5(c) contains only the interim certification and no cure or repurchase remedy; only 5(d) supplies one. The cross-reference cannot be squared with what those subsections actually say.

The first clause qualifies the schedule's accuracy 'in all material respects', but the second warrants that 'all information supplied by, on behalf of, or concerning the Mortgagor is true, accurate and complete' — an unbounded, unqualified representation about information the HELOC Seller did not generate. The reach of 'concerning the Mortgagor' and the mismatched materiality qualifiers are both open.

This representation warrants that 'the proceeds of the Revolving Credit Loan have been fully disbursed and there is no requirement for future advances thereunder', which cannot be reconciled with Section 2(a) (additional balances from future Draws) or Section 7(xx) (each loan has a 5, 10 or 15 year Draw Period). The assets sold are revolving lines of credit by definition.

This clause warrants that 'upon recordation the Purchaser or its designee will be the owner of record', but Sections 4(b) and 6(a) require the assignments of the Security Instrument to be recorded to the Indenture Trustee, not the Purchaser. Who becomes owner of record is left inconsistent across the instrument.

'all applicable predatory, abusive and fair lending laws' is an open-ended catch-all appended to a specific list (usury, equal credit opportunity, disclosure, recording), and 'abusive' lending laws is not a recognised statutory category. Its reach against the enumerated specifics is uncertain.

The clause uses two different delinquency yardsticks in a single sentence — 'not delinquent in payment more than 29 days' now, and 'no payment has been 30 days delinquent during the preceding twelve month period' — without saying how days delinquent are counted. Whether a loan one cycle behind breaches is open.

This clause warrants there is 'no default, breach, violation or event of acceleration existing under any Mortgage', while Section 7(f) expressly tolerates loans delinquent in payment by up to 29 days. A payment delinquency is ordinarily a default, so the two representations pull apart.

The clause refers to terms 'reflected in the Revolving Credit Loan Schedule', a document nowhere defined, while Section 3 creates and defines the 'Mortgage Loan Schedule'. Whether they are the same list has to be worked out from the rest of the instrument.

The representation is qualified by what was 'reasonably believed by the HELOC Seller' to be adverse, mixing a subjective belief with an objective reasonableness standard and giving no benchmark for an adverse selection procedure. What counts as a prohibited 'selection procedure' is undefined.

The permitted title exceptions end with '(iii) other matters to which like properties are commonly subject which do not materially interfere with the benefits of the security', a catch-all whose reach against the enumerated exceptions (i) and (ii) is uncertain. 'Commonly subject' and 'materially interfere' are both unmeasured.

The clause addresses only first lien and 'second lien' Revolving Credit Loans, while the Preamble and the definition of 'Mortgage' cover HELOCs secured by any 'first or junior lien'. Loans in a third or lower lien position fall outside the representation.

The representation opens 'with respect to each junior lien Revolving Credit Loan' but its operative language then speaks of 'the mortgagee under the second lien Revolving Credit Loan'. Whether the notice-and-cure warranty extends beyond second liens to all junior liens is genuinely unclear.

'free of material damage', 'in good repair' and the qualifier 'to the best of the HELOC Seller's knowledge' — which is attached only to the litigation limb — leave the condition warranted and the knowledge qualifier's reach both unfixed. Whether the property-condition limbs are absolute or knowledge-qualified is arguable.

The obligation applies only 'where required or customary in the jurisdiction in which the Mortgaged Property is located', a customary-practice qualifier with no ascertainable content. Whether the request-for-notice filing was required is left to evidence outside the contract.

This clause requires hazard insurance by 'an insurer acceptable under the Fannie Mae Guides', while Section 7(z) warrants insurance by 'an insurer which is acceptable to the HELOC Seller' with a different amount test. Two representations set different insurance standards for the same properties.

'other assurance of title customary in the relevant jurisdiction therefor in a form acceptable to Fannie Mae or Freddie Mac' and the alternative that '(b) a lien search was conducted' leave what actually satisfies the junior-lien title requirement uncertain. The $200,000 Piggyback Loan carve-out further complicates which loans the warranty reaches.

'Qualified Appraiser' is capitalized but nowhere defined in this Agreement, so the standard the appraiser must meet is imported from an unstated source. The balance of the clause then supplies its own Fannie/Freddie/FIRREA test.

This clause warrants an appraisal conforming to 'the underwriting requirements of the originator', while Section 7(x) warrants an appraisal satisfying Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac and Title XI of FIRREA. Two overlapping appraisal representations set different benchmarks for the same appraisal.

The insurer need only be 'acceptable to the HELOC Seller' here, whereas Section 7(v) requires an insurer 'acceptable under the Fannie Mae Guides' and a flood policy meeting Federal Insurance Administration guidelines. The two insurance representations impose inconsistent standards.

The REMIC 'qualified mortgage' representation sits in a transaction the recitals describe as a Delaware statutory trust issuing notes under an Indenture, with no REMIC election referred to anywhere in the Agreement. Whether this tax representation has any operative field is a whole-instrument question.

After the enumerated categories ('high cost home', 'covered', 'high risk home', 'predatory') the clause adds 'or a similarly classified loan using different terminology under a law imposing heightened regulatory scrutiny or additional legal liability'. The reach of that catch-all against the specific list is exactly the ejusdem generis problem.

The clause warrants information in 'Schedule A of the Prospectus Supplement', while Schedule A to this Agreement is the Required Ratings schedule and Section 5(c) uses 'Schedule A' for an exception list to the interim certification. The same label carries three referents across the instrument.

The clause ties the definitions to 'the then current Standard & Poor's LEVELS Glossary, which is now Version 5.6c', leaving unclear whether the version current at origination, at closing, or Version 5.6c attached as Exhibit 6 governs. The parenthesis is also never closed.

'the underwriting guidelines of the related originator' is not identified, dated or attached, and the clause says nothing about permitted exceptions to those guidelines. What compliance means, and against which version of which originator's guidelines, is left open.

The clause accepts that a Mortgage may merely be 'in the process of being recorded' in accordance with Section 2.01 of the Sale and Servicing Agreement, while Section 6(a) of this Agreement sets a 180-day outside recording date with its own exceptions. The recording standard differs between the two provisions.

This clause measures the Mortgage File against 'Section 2.01 of the Sale and Servicing Agreement', whereas Section 1 defines 'Mortgage File' by reference to Exhibit 1 to this Agreement and Sections 5(c)-(d) review against Exhibit 1. Which list controls the contents of the file is unresolved.

This clause fixes Minimum Monthly Payments as 'due and payable on the first day of each month', while the Section 1 definition of Due Date makes the payment date whatever 'the related Mortgage Note' says. The two cannot both fix the payment date.

The clause warrants that the assignment is 'in recordable form and (other than with respect to the blank assignee) is acceptable for recording', which concedes the assignee is left blank while asserting recordability. Whether an assignment in blank satisfies the warranty is genuinely contestable.

The proviso — 'no residence or dwelling is a single parcel of real property with a cooperative housing corporation erected thereon, or a mobile home' — is garbled and does not track the property types just enumerated. What it excludes is not clear on the face of the clause.

The clause warrants that each prepayment penalty 'is at least equal to the lesser of (A) the maximum amount permitted under applicable law and (B) six months interest', which sets a floor where a cap is plainly intended and would warrant penalties at the legal maximum. Read literally it contradicts the same clause's assurance that each penalty 'is permitted pursuant to federal, state and local law'.

This clause requires that a leasehold's remaining term 'does not terminate less than ten years after the maturity date' of the HELOC, while Section 7(zz)(ix) requires a ground lease term extending only 'at least five years beyond the maturity date'. The two leasehold representations set incompatible minimum terms.

'customary and enforceable provisions such as to render the rights and remedies of the holder thereof adequate' states no ascertainable standard for adequacy or custom. Whether a given mortgage form satisfies it can only be argued.

Limb (B) offers four alternatives ending with '(4) not doing business in such state', which swallows the licensing and qualification requirements that limbs (A) and (B)(1)-(3) impose. The relationship between the general escape and the enumerated specifics is uncertain.

This clause and Section 7(jjj) both warrant that the Mortgagor received all required disclosure materials, the latter adding an executed statement and a file-retention duty. Two overlapping representations on the same subject invite argument about which controls.

The representation turns on 'any circumstances or condition ... that could reasonably be expected to cause investors to regard the Revolving Credit Loan as an unacceptable investment', a standard with no ascertainable boundary and referable to an unidentified body of investors. The clause also repeats the bankruptcy limb twice ('is not in bankruptcy and, the Mortgagor is not insolvent or in bankruptcy').

This clause warrants a monthly-adjusting rate equal to Index plus Gross Margin subject to caps, while Section 1 defines 'Mortgage Rate' as 'the annual rate of interest borne by a Mortgage Note as stated herein' and builds Net Mortgage Rate on it. The rate architecture in the definitions does not fit the adjustable rate warranted here.

'each Revolving Credit Loan requires the payment of a Cancellation Fee, where applicable' is circular: the qualifier 'where applicable' removes whatever content the warranty had. Nothing in the Agreement says when a Cancellation Fee is applicable or what it is.

The clause says each loan matures in either 180 or 300 months and has a Draw Period of 5, 10 or 15 years followed by a ten-year Amortization Period, but a 10-year draw plus 10-year amortization equals 240 months, which is neither permitted term. The two sentences cannot both be true of a 10-year-draw loan.

The list of eligible originators ends with 'or similar institution which is supervised and examined by a federal or state authority', a catch-all whose reach against the enumerated institutions is uncertain. Whether a licensed non-bank mortgage lender qualifies is exactly the ejusdem generis question.

Limb (ix) requires the ground lease term to extend 'at least five years beyond the maturity date', while Section 7(mm) requires a leasehold not to terminate 'less than ten years after the maturity date' of the HELOC. The two leasehold representations set different minimum terms for the same collateral.

Eligibility is measured against 'HELOC Seller's Underwriting Standards', while Section 7(ee) warrants origination in accordance with 'the underwriting guidelines of the related originator' and the recitals show the loans were originated and serviced by others. Which set of standards governs a condominium or PUD loan is unresolved.

'no claims will arise as to broker fees that are double charged' is a warranty about future events by third parties, and 'properly assessed' has no stated benchmark. What breach of this clause looks like, and when, is unclear.

The proviso caps lost note affidavits at 1% 'of the Revolving Credit Loans, in the aggregate', a pool-level test embedded in loan-level representations whose only remedy is loan-by-loan cure, repurchase or substitution under the Section 7 repurchase provision. It is also uncertain how it interacts with Section 4(b)(iii) and the Exhibit 5 schedule of lost notes, which permit affidavits without any stated cap.

This clause warrants that the loan documents 'have been delivered to the Purchaser or its designee', while Section 4(b) requires delivery to the Indenture Trustee or the Custodian and permits a later Mortgage File Delivery Date. The 'except as provided in Section 4(b)' carve-out does not clearly resolve to whom delivery must be made.

This clause duplicates the disclosure warranty already given in Section 7(rr), adding a signed statement and a Servicing File retention duty. Whether the two clauses impose one obligation or two is left to construction.

For a second lien loan the clause warrants no uncured 'notice of default of a junior lien', which is backwards: the risk to a second lien holder is default under the senior lien, as Section 7(s)(3) and 7(m) confirm. The mistaken word changes what the representation covers.

'a higher-cost product designed for less creditworthy borrowers' and the exception for borrowers who 'did not qualify ... for a lower cost credit product' set no measurable test for steering. The clause also misspells 'debit-to-income' for debt-to-income.

'the principal determining factor' and 'a reasonable ability to make timely payments' are both unquantified standards applied to an underwriting methodology that is never identified. Whether a stated-income HELOC breaches this clause is squarely a matter of construction.

This clause warrants that 'no Revolving Credit Loan is subject to negative amortization', yet Section 7(w) requires every title policy to 'contain all applicable endorsements including a negative amortization endorsement, if applicable'. The instrument both denies and contemplates negative amortization.

The clause warrants the past and ongoing credit-reporting conduct of 'the Servicer', a term this Agreement never defines and which the recitals identify as GreenPoint, a non-party. Whose conduct EMC is warranting has to be worked out from the rest of the instrument.

This paragraph makes the Section 7 representations inure to 'the Purchaser, its successors and assigns' without qualification, while the recital on assignment says the representations and remedies pass to the Issuer only 'to the extent provided in the related Assignment Agreement'. Who holds the benefit of the warranties is left to be reconciled.

The proviso turns on 'a breach of the representation contained in clause CD) of this Section 7', a cross-reference that does not correspond to any lettered clause, so the second trigger for the prepayment-charge alternative remedy cannot be identified. The 90-day clock also runs from the earlier of the Seller's own 'discovery' or notice, leaving the trigger for the repurchase obligation contestable.

This repurchase protocol (notice, 90 days, cure/repurchase/substitute) overlaps with Section 5(d), which imposes its own separate Material Defect notice, 90-day cure and repurchase regime for missing or defective documents that the Section 7(gg) and 7(hhh) representations also cover. Which protocol governs a document breach is unresolved.

The clause makes a cause of action accrue only on the Seller's 'discovery' of a breach plus its failure to cure, repurchase or substitute, rather than on the making of the false representation. Whether that language postpones accrual — and the limitations period — is precisely what parties fight over.

Section 7 states that the representations are made 'as of the Closing Date', so a breach exists at closing, while this paragraph defers accrual until discovery and failure to cure. The two cannot easily be harmonised.

The clause warrants about 'the HELOC Seller's Information (as defined in Section 13(a) hereof)', but the table of contents makes Section 13 the indemnification section and Exhibit 3 separately carries the HELOC Seller's Information. The content of the warranted information depends on a cross-reference that must be checked against Section 13 and Exhibit 3.

The condition that the representations 'shall be true and correct as of the date or dates specified in all material respects' misplaces the materiality qualifier and leaves the 'date or dates specified' unidentified. What must be true, and when, is not clear from the sentence.

Section 10 sets out the conditions to the Purchaser's obligations, but Section 2(a) conditions the purchase and sale on 'the conditions set forth in Section 11 hereof' while Section 2(c) cites Section 10. Which section supplies the closing conditions is inconsistent across the instrument.

The clause promises 'all of the following closing documents' but no list follows in the instrument, and the only standard given is documents 'in such forms as are agreed upon and reasonably acceptable to the Purchaser'. What must be delivered as a condition to closing is therefore indeterminate.
